root_idea.summary: The root centers on being fixed, stationary, or firmly established, and on causing something to become so.
root_idea.development: Its lexical development extends from remaining firm or settled to anchoring ships, fixing objects, designating places or times of anchoring, and figurative settling or remaining.

senses.definition: To make firm, fixed, or firmly established.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive use whose Quranic object is the mountains; the sense concerns causing them to be firmly set.

senses.definition: The place or state of anchoring; an anchorage or place where something comes to rest.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression concerning the ship, it denotes its anchorage or being brought to rest.

senses.definition: The appointed time of being established or of an event taking place.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of the appointed time or arrival of an event, especially the eschatological Hour.

senses.definition: Firmly fixed, stationary, or immovable; in the Quran, firmly set mountains and fixed cooking pots.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic group is chiefly the plural رَوَاسِي and also includes رَاسِيَات; the same fixedness is applied to mountains and, in one passage, to large cooking pots that remain in place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become stationary, fixed, firm, steady, or steadfast; of a foot, to stand firm in combat, and of a mountain, to be firmly based.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general intransitive use describing remaining firmly in place or maintaining firmness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a ship, to anchor, lie at anchor, or become stationary by grounding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ship may rest on its anchor or remain stationary when its lower part reaches the bottom.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a stallion-camel, to leap upon his she-camels; alternatively, to bray to them so that they turn toward him and become still.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized camel-herding expression with variant explanations of the stallion's action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bring about agreement, harmony, reconciliation, accommodation, or adjustment between people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a group or party as the object of the reconciliation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To mention a portion of a report or story, or to relate a report as received from and attributed to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may express attribution to an informant or relating the report inwardly to oneself.
A specialized use with fasting as the intended action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A part or portion of a tradition, report, or story.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use referring to a section of transmitted discourse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bracelet made of strung beads or turtle-shell, including a particular type of bead bracelet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete noun for an ornamental bracelet; its reported plural is رَسَوَات.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Firm or steadfast in good or evil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of steadfast character or condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The pole fixed in the middle of a tent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized concrete use referring to a tent's fixed central support.
A Form III reciprocal or associative construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a thing stationary or firm; especially, to anchor or ground a ship and make it fast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative transitive use applied particularly to ships and anchors.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A verbal noun or a noun of time or place; as a place, an anchorage, port, or station for ships.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form can designate the act, time, or place of coming to rest, with the place sense especially associated with ships.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The anchor of a ship, especially a large anchor that holds the ship fast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A concrete nautical noun; the anchor is lowered into the water and tied by ropes to prevent the ship from proceeding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression أَلْقَوْا مَرَاسِيَهُمْ, to remain, stay, dwell, or abide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative idiom based on casting anchors.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression أَلْقَتِ السَّحَابَةُ مَرَاسِيَهَا, for a cloud to remain steady or stationary while raining, or to rain continually.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative cloud expression combining settled stillness with sustained rain.
